At 4.30p.m. 5-5-41, one of the men named
Yao Loh (姚六) alias Yao Chih Yue
(姚志餘), 46, Zangzok, M/basket shop-
master, 3 Kao Chao Lee, Sinza Road,
wanted on Circular Order of Arrest No. 638 issued
by the S.S.D. Court 9-10-40 (See Diaries 9 & 10),
surrendered himself to this Station, in company
with Lawyer Tao Wu Chih (陶培志), residing at 138/31
Tatung Road. This wanted man now becomes the 6th
accused in this case.

As shown in Diary 2, the 6th accused was implicated
by the 1st & 2nd accused as being an accomplice, who,
concerned with others, took away the complainant's
money and property.

Questioned by C.I.C. 38 and the undersigned, the
accused however, strongly denied being a participant
in this offence.

He has been charged with Unarmed Highway Robbery
and will be brought before the S.S.D. Court a.m.

My name is Tse Ling Hoong, age 27, and native of Taichow.
I am a coolie by profession and I have no fixed abode.
At 6 p.m. 4/9/40, I walked along Tatung Road where I saw
one named Wong Yee (3rd accused), sitting inside a tea house
at 543, Tatung Road. At 9.45 p.m. even date, one named Liu
Vung Kwe, a former acquaintance of mine called me to accompany
him to a jetty off Tatung Road to remove some scrap brass.
I immediately proceeded there, when I saw a number of persons,
and the 3rd accused, who was dressed in Foreign style clothes,
holding a baton in his hand and told some one that he was a
detective, attached to The Floating Restaurant. Shortly
afters, Liu Vung Kwe carried two sacks of brass discharged from
a boat and told me to remove the same to a house, situated
at 543 Tatung Road, which I did. Liu Vung Kwei later gave
me 50 / and stated that the brass had been taken away by the
3rd accused. On 8/9/40 I was arrested by the Police. At about
6 p.m. 13/9/40 I was removed from the station cells for an
identification parade, I recognised a fat man amongst them as
the person who wore foreign style clothes at the time of the
occurrence and who represented himself as a detective attached
to the Floating Restaurant.
(Sd) Tse Ling Hoeng.

我叫谢灵洪，27岁，泰州人。

1940年9月4日下午6点，我沿着大同路行走，看到一名叫王义（Wong Yee，第三被告）的人坐在大同路543号的一家茶馆里。同日晚上9点45分，我的一位旧相识刘云贵（Liu Vung Kwe）叫我和他一起去大同路外的一个码头搬运一些废铜。我立即前往那里，看到许多人，第三被告身穿西式服装，手里拿着一根警棍，告诉某人他是隶属于浮游餐厅的侦探。不久之后，刘云贵搬了两袋从船上卸下的铜，让我把它们搬到位于大同路543号的一所房子里，我照做了。后来刘云贵给了我50分，并说铜已被第三被告拿走。1940年9月8日，我被警察逮捕。1940年9月13日下午6点左右，我被从捕房牢房带出进行列队辨认，我认出其中一名胖子就是事发时身穿西式服装并自称是浮游餐厅侦探的人。

My name is Wong Kyung, age 51, and native of Kompo. I
am married and live at 10 Yien Ching Li, Chengtu Road. I am
a member of the Special Service Section of the Garrison Corps,

At 7 p.m. 4/9/40, whilst in a teashop at 543 Tatung Road,
I met my friend Tsai Ts Kwong, and he told me to go with him
to seize smuggled goods at a jetty off Soochow Road.
At about 9.30 p.m. he led me, Liu Van Kwei, one named
Dzoong, and 3 or 4 others unknown to me, to a jetty off
Soochow Road near Markham Road Bridge. Tsai Ts Kwong stated
that they had come from The Floating Restaurant (The office of
Japanese Gendarmerie) to seize smuggled goods, pushed the
complainant away and instructed Liu Van Kwei to tell the
unknown persons to take away 5 sacks of scrap brass.
(5/9/40)
On the following day I met Tsai Ts Kwong, and he told
me that the property had been disposed of by Liu Van Kwei,
and that Liu had absconded because Liu had heard that the
report
complainant intended to report case to the Police. Therefore
I had not received any proceeds.
This is a true statement.
(Sd) Wong Kyung.

我叫王京，51岁，高邮人。我已婚，居住在成都路延庆里10号。我是警卫队特工科的一员，该科位于极司菲尔路（Jessfield Road）62号孔家角（Kong Ka Jau）。
1940年9月4日晚上7点，当我在大同路543号的一家茶馆时，遇到了我的朋友蔡芝光，他让我和他一起去苏州路外的一个码头查扣走私货物。
晚上9点30分左右，他带领我、刘万贵（Liu Van Kwei）、一名姓钟（Dzoong）的人以及我不认识的三四个人，来到靠近马克姆路（Markham Road）桥的苏州路外的一个码头。蔡芝光声称他们来自浮游餐厅（日本宪兵队办公室）查扣走私货物，推开投诉人，并指示刘万贵让那些不认识的人拿走5袋废铜。
（1940年9月5日）
第二天我遇到蔡芝光，他告诉我财物已由刘万贵处理，刘万贵因听说投诉人打算向警方报案而潜逃。因此我没有收到任何所得。
此陈述属实。

page_data.en:
At 9.30a.m. 6-9-40, the complainant Too Ching
Lee (吳正礼) of H.F.A., now occupying Room 14,
Yung An (永安) Lodging House, 104 Shunteh Road,
reported that he had been held up by 5 or 6 men
described overleaf, who robbed him of $15.00 in
notes and a quantity of brass wires, brass & tin
ingots, total value $515.00.

Inquiries by C.D.S. 67 and the undersigned
ascertained that the complainant was a brass shop
keeper in Yangchow, and owing to depression of
trade, he closed down his shop and conveyed the
stock to Shanghai by boat, with the intention of
disposing of same.

At about 10p.m. 4-9-40, after the boat had
arrived at Shanghai and tied up to a public jetty
off West Soochow Road, opposite the Sinsa Depot,
P.W.D. between Markham Road Bridge and Tatung Road,
the complainant and a fellow countryman named Tsu
Vung Yuen (蔡元) brought the brass wires, brass
& tin ingots contained in two sacks to the roadway
leading from steps of the jetty, where they were
approached by 5 or 6 unknown persons. The 1st
described man alleged that he was coming from the
Floating Restaurant, on The Bund (now the office of
a Japanese Gendarmerie) accused the complainant of
transporting smuggled goods, and demanded the
payment of $200.00 as "landing tax".

The complainant refused to pay them any money,
whereupon the culprits searched his person and
took away a sum of $15.00 from his belt-pocket.
page_data.zh:
1940年9月6日上午9:30，现居住于顺德里104号永安旅馆14室的英籍华人 (H.F.A.) 吴正礼 (Too Ching Lee) 报案称，他被前述的五或六名男子拦截，抢走面值15.00元的纸币以及一批黄铜丝、黄铜锭和锡锭，总价值515.00元.

经刑事侦缉处 (C.D.S.) 67号警员及本人调查查明，报案人是扬州的一家铜器店店主，因生意萧条，他关闭了店铺，并用船将库存货物运至上海，意图出售.

1940年9月4日晚上10点左右，船只抵达上海并停靠在西苏州路公共码头，该码头位于工务局 (P.W.D.) 新沙仓库 (Sinsa Depot) 对面，介于马克姆路桥和大通路之间，报案人与一名名叫蔡元 (Tsu Vung Yuen) 的同乡将装有黄铜丝、黄铜锭和锡锭的两个麻袋搬至从码头台阶通往道路的路口，此时有五或六名不明身份的人接近他们. 上述第一名男子声称他来自外滩的浮游餐厅（现为日本宪兵队办公室），指控报案人运输走私货物，并要求支付200.00元作为“上岸税”.

报案人拒绝向他们支付任何钱款，于是罪犯搜查了他的身体，并从他的腰带口袋中拿走了15.00元.

Evidently dis-satisfied with the amount of money stolen,
they removed the 2 sacks & contents and escaped in an easterly
direction along West Soochow Road, turning South on
Tatung Road, where the complainant lost sight of them.
The complainant did not raise an alarm as he had
been threatened that if he did so, his life would be
in danger.
Nearest policeman to the scene was C.P.C. 2030 on
duty at 3 Post (Kirkham Road Bridge) at a distance of
about 60 yards away, and he knew nothing of the
robbery, since the complainant failed to cry out for
help.
The complainant had not been to Shanghai before and
on advice of a relative named Zung Yung Foo (陳永福)
residing at 738 Canton Road, made this report to Police
after 2 days had elapsed.
He was taken to nearby teashops, but did not identify
any of the visitors as having participated in the
robbery, it being suspected that this offence was
perpetrated by loafers, on the pretext of being
members of the Japanese Gendarmerie.
Complainant was shown photographs of the recently
released prisoners, but no identification was effected.
Likely places of disposal will be visited to trace
the stolen property. Circulated.
Enquiries proceeding.

报案人没有发出警报，因为他受到威胁，如果这样做，他的生命将有危险.
离现场最近的警察是第3岗（柯克姆路/Kirkham Road 桥）执勤的中央巡捕房警员 (C.P.C.) 2030号，距离约60码，由于报案人没有呼救，他对抢劫案一无所知.
报案人以前从未到过上海，在居住在广东路738号的亲戚陈永福 (Zung Yung Foo) 的建议下，他在两天后才向警方报案.
他被带到附近的茶馆，但未能指认任何访客参与抢劫，怀疑此案由游手好闲之徒作案，借口是日本宪兵队成员.
